Given a representation $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$, we define:
\begin{itemize}
\item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi$ is the $C^*$-algebra homomorphism, \[\pi_e:=\rho\circ\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)\] of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$, where $\rho$ is the canonical proyection of $B(H)$ onto the Calkin Algebra $B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)$.
\item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi$ is the restriction,
\begin{align*}
\pi_d:ker(\pi_e)&\to \mathcal{K}(H)\\
a &\to \pi(a)
\end{align*}
\item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is defined in the following way:
\[\pi(\mathcal{A})_d:=\pi(\mathcal{A})\cap \mathcal{K}(H).\]
\item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is the image $\pi(\mathcal{A})_e$ of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ in the Calkin Algebra. 
\item The \textit{essential part} of $H$ is defined in the following way:
\[H_e:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)\]
\item The \textit{discrete part} of $H$ is defined in the following way:
\[H_d:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)^\perp\]
\item The \textit{essential part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_e$ of $v$ over $H_e$.
\item The \textit{discrete part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_d$ of $v$ over $H_d$.
\item The \textit{essential part} of a set $E\subseteq H$ is the set
\[E_e:=\{v_e\ |\ v\in E\}\]
\item The \textit{discrete part} of a set $G\subseteq H$ is the set
\[E_d:=\{v_d\ |\ v\in G\}\]
\end{itemize}
